finding.claim: Unvalidated stored callbackUrl from subscribe() is passed to URI.create and sent a POST by notifyAll(), enabling blind SSRF to arbitrary http/https internal hosts.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe() (documented as POST /subscribe), src/Jobs.java:12-13
finding.sink: URI.create(cb) and client.send(req, ...) in notifyAll(), src/Jobs.java:21 and :24

trace.note: notifyAll iterates all stored callback values every minute
client.send; response body discarded, so blind SSRF

finding.guards_checked: No validation at store time (src/Jobs.java:13-14) or send time (src/Jobs.java:19-24). Java HttpClient limits schemes to http/https. newHttpClient() default redirect policy is NEVER, so no redirect-based bypass, but direct http:// targets to internal hosts (e.g. 169.254.169.254, localhost) remain reachable. Route auth for /subscribe is not in this repo and is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. No validation at store time (src/Jobs.java:13-14) or send time (src/Jobs.java:19-24). The regex check at src/Jobs.java:30 is in thumb() and does not apply to notifyAll().
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code (src/Jobs.java:13-14, 19-24), and no closing guard exists on the notifyAll() path, but the source is only a comment saying "POST /subscribe" (src/Jobs.java:12), and the route, its auth, and who can reach it are not in this repo, so I cannot confirm an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker controls callbackUrl.
